bound.note: EXACT for the canonical two-query construction; therefore only an UPPER bound on the minimum. pin-0/pin-1 needs 2 where the canonical query uses 4, and FED-MIN-GROWS makes the gap unbounded. Citing this for a lower bound is refused by scripts/check-claim-ledger.mjs.

attrs.evidence: Each canonical conjunctive query emits one atom per tuple of each relation, so it has Σ|R^A| constraints over |D| variables; two of them glued at the free variable give 2Σ|R^A| constraints over 2|D|−1 variables. Verified as an EQUALITY on the constraint count for six languages, including the case that motivated the question: {≠∘f, NAE₃} over |D|=3 has |≠∘f| = 4 and |NAE₃| = 27−3 = 24, so 2(4+24) = 56 — exactly the refutation whose size defeated the round-3 exhaustive space. THIS RETIRES THE FRONTIER QUESTION AS ASKED. Round 3 asked whether any finite bound exists on a minimal witness; the construction it already shipped is one, and nobody had computed it. The live questions are tightness, worst-case minimum as a function of |D| and the signature, lower-bound families, and whether a smaller orbit-separating pp-formula can be extracted than the full canonical query. R4.1 ADDED THE POLARITY FIELD, because this record was misused within one revision of being written: R3.1 cited it for a growing MINIMUM. The claim itself was and is correct; the defect was downstream, and the ledger can now refuse that direction mechanically.
attrs.prior_art: Derived by GPT-5.6 in the round-4 audit from the canonical-query construction already in scripts/federation-kernel.mjs. Canonical databases are standard (Chandra–Merlin 1977).
attrs.review_focus: The bound is the canonical construction's exact size, so as a bound on the MINIMUM it is only an upper one, and the pin-0/pin-1 case shows it can be loose by a factor. A worst-case lower-bound family is what would make it sharp.
attrs.statement: If the core of (D; Γ) has at least two automorphism orbits, a refutation of split-cycle sufficiency exists with exactly 2·Σ_{R∈Γ}|R^A| constraints over at most 2|D|−1 variables.
